tags: Encrypted communities with text and voice. No host required. Your keys, your fleet.
content:
Armada is a community chat app with servers, channels, and voice, where your
keys are your identity and no one has to run anything.

Spin up a Concord: a serverless, end-to-end encrypted community. Nothing to
set up, and only members can read it — not the relays that carry it. Text
channels, live voice rooms, and invites, all without a host.

Prefer full control? Self-host an Armada server on your own infrastructure
and own the whole stack: membership, moderation, and data.

Features:
- End-to-end encrypted communities (Concord), no server to run
- Voice rooms with encrypted group calls and DM calls
- Discord-style servers and channels, self-hostable
- Portable identity: sign in with your key on any device

Fix proposal base selection for PR pushes and draft patches, refresh dependencies,
and clarify agent guidance for repository data refreshes.

### Changed

- Refresh Rust dependencies and the lockfile, including Nostr SDK 0.45.4,
  Reqwest 0.13.5, Rustls 0.23.45, apk-info 1.0.13, mailparse 0.17.0,
  keyring 4.2.0, and the test harness dependencies. Relevant upstream fixes:
  - Rustls rejects TLS 1.3 handshake messages received at the wrong encryption
    level ([GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/releases/tag/v%2F0.23.45)).
  - Reqwest selects the correct credentials when multiple proxies match a URL
    and recognizes timeouts wrapped in response-body decoding errors
    ([release notes](https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/releases/tag/v0.13.5)).
  - APK analysis can continue when the resource table is corrupt, resolves
    sparse resource entries correctly, and reads ZIP entries lazily to reduce
    memory use with large archives
    ([release notes](https://github.com/delvinru/apk-info/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1013---2026-09-10)).
  - The Nostr SDK's local relay, used by the test harness, closes subscriptions
    when their live-event buffer overflows so clients can detect missing events
    ([crate changelog](https://docs.rs/crate/nostr-sdk/0.45.4/source/CHANGELOG.md)).
- Clarify the agent skill's shared repository-data refresh behavior across git
  and ngit commands, and when to reuse cached data with `--offline` to avoid
  redundant relay fetching.

### Fixed

- Fix PR pushes when changes are already on your local default branch or
  another remote but have not been accepted by the Nostr destination.
  A PR that points to the same commit as local `main` or `master` works too.
- Support maintainers who build PRs on a newer local default branch. For a new
  PR sharing local commits that have not been published to Nostr, explain how
  `-o base=<commit-or-ref>` chooses where the proposed changes start. Earlier
  commits remain in Git history. Local changes outside the PR need no confirmation.
- Keep `ngit send` working for drafts made directly on `main` or `master`.
  Rejection messages explain how `--base <commit-or-ref>` lets you choose
  which earlier commits to exclude. Remote names such as `origin` or `github`
  do not establish ownership or accepted history.

tags: Nostr-native Git collaboration from the command line.
content:
ngit is a command-line client and Git remote helper for decentralized code
collaboration over Nostr. It keeps repository state, issues, and pull
requests on Nostr while using interchangeable Git servers for object
storage.

# Private Provider 0.7.3

Private Provider is a phone-first AI workspace for Android (ARM64). It runs a
bundled local runtime with `routstrd` and the Pi coding agent, pays for
inference with a built-in Cashu wallet, and publishes projects through ngit
with an external Amber signer.

## What's changed

- **The project folder now shows which draft you are on.** The status line names
  the branch it is describing — for example
  `fix/list-clients-last-used · 1 commit to push` — so it is clear what the
  "ahead" or "behind" figure refers to.
- **A "Go to main" button.** When a project is on a pull-request or feature
  draft instead of the default branch, the project page offers a one-tap return
  to the default branch. It is a plain local checkout: it does not fetch, push,
  or sign, and it refuses to run while you have uncommitted changes.

Everything from 0.7.2 is included:

- **Pi can ask the app to perform ngit actions.** Ask Pi to open a pull request,
  post a comment, add a label, or file an issue; the app shows the exact
  command, you approve, and Amber signs. Merge, push-to-main, close and resolve
  are offered only for repositories you maintain. Pi never receives your
  signing key.
- **New ngit runtime (ngit 3.0.3, runtime 0.1.8)** — fixes PR pushes when the
  change is already committed on your default branch, and keeps multi-line PR
  descriptions intact.
- **Accurate project sync status**, plus push and preview safety fixes: a
  conflicted merge is never reported as success, and the PR preview no longer
  modifies your Git index.

## Runtime

- Bundled runtime **0.1.8** (ngit **3.0.3**). The optional on-device build
  toolchain is unchanged (toolchain 1).

## Requirements

- Android 8.0 or newer (API 26+) on an **ARM64** device.
- About 185 MB download and roughly 2 GB free storage on first launch.
- A small Bitcoin/Lightning balance for paid inference.

## Known limitations — please read

- **Wallet recovery is not available.** Keep only small amounts.
- **Non-attested models** are served by third-party providers that can read the
  prompt.
- Pi sessions and Workspace files are not additionally encrypted by the app.
- Background work uses a foreground service; swiping the app from recents closes
  it and cancels in-flight requests. Some manufacturers' battery managers may
  still stop background work.
- **After you send a change as a pull request**, the app returns you to the
  draft you were on, and that draft still holds the change locally — so it can
  keep reading "1 commit to push" even though the pull request is open. That is
  the local copy, not the pull request. Use **Go to main** to return to the
  default branch; the pull request itself is unaffected.

## Verify what you install

- APK: `private-provider-0.7.3-274-product.apk`
- SHA-256: `a19da920f8698e392ef03cf4c2836d9328733e0bafe0ffd2da912e3165a0dc84`
- Signing certificate SHA-256:
  `2b356f863d6d752ca7767c68251fea91ab85a2f4ca33366f973bcb37c59bacfa`

Future updates will be signed with the same certificate. See
`INSTALL-AND-VERIFY.md` for step-by-step verification and installation.

## Licenses

The app source is GPL-3.0-or-later (`LICENSE`). Bundled native components keep
their own licenses; see `licenses/`, including the written source offer for
PRoot (GPL-2.0) and talloc (LGPL-3.0).

content:
## Archipelago 1.8.22-alpha

App lifecycle and readiness fixes, persistent Gitea/Portainer and Nginx Proxy Manager repairs, kiosk improvements, and Angor services.

- Installed apps stay visible through restarts and refreshes. Launch readiness checks the correct web interface; Bitcoin's dashboard remains available during initial sync.
- Fixed Nginx Proxy Manager admin-port selection and bind-address health checks. Recognized legacy tunnel/LND port conflicts receive a backed-up migration.
- Network diagnostic failures no longer stop all apps or reset shared container networking. Missing companion dashboards are recovered only by their owning service.
- Persistent Gitea/Portainer connectivity repair preserves application state and supports fresh installation and upgrades.
- Readable Bitcoin version and pruning choices in the kiosk; compact named readiness messages, aligned card buttons, and one Mempool card.
- Restored GitWorkshop build files and companion image sources. Runtime files finish promotion before app manifests are loaded.
- Paid-file delivery and repeat-download improvements, including live Tor-only purchase, change, rejection refund and file-content verification.
- Added headless Angor Indexer using Mempool/ElectrumX, with a separate optional relay. A full, unpruned Bitcoin node and completed downstream indexing are required for full availability.
- Retains prior Cashu, Lightning startup/balance, explorer, pruning, graceful shutdown and transparent AIUI fixes.

### Validation

1,617 backend tests and 1,133 frontend tests passed; four backend tests requiring optional external services or hardware were excluded. Container, migration, installer-overlay, app build-context and release checks passed. Live acceptance covered the development box and ThinkPad X250, including the actual Chromium kiosk and Portainer's network namespace. Bitcoin/LND and the existing production site were preserved during final management updates.

The raw ISO passed payload comparison and a complete offline UEFI installation and installed-system cold boot in QEMU/KVM, reaching the first-run setup screen.

Full-chain Angor indexing is still awaiting the development node's initial Bitcoin synchronization. No claim of completed chain indexing or testing on every hardware configuration is made.

### Downloads

Use the OTA from Settings for an existing installation. For a fresh installation, download the raw `.iso` asset, together with its SHA-256 and signed checksum JSON. The ISO is not compressed as `.zst`.

tags: A Nostr-powered personal cloud and self-hosted AI — notes, calendar, contacts, files, passwords
content:
PosterChan is the Android half of a **Nostr-powered personal cloud** and a **self-hosted AI powerhouse**
that runs on hardware you own. Your notes, calendar, contacts, files, passwords and mail live as encrypted
Nostr events on a relay you run — no account with anybody, no subscription, no vendor holding the keys.

**The personal cloud**

- **Notes**: private, offline-first, encrypted to your own key. Write with no signal; it syncs when you have one.
- **Calendar and contacts**: real **CalDAV/CardDAV**, so your phone's own calendar and contacts apps sync
  with your node like any other server — one account for both.
- **Files and folder sync**: keep Documents and Pictures in step between phone and desktop through your own
  node. Contents are encrypted before they leave the device, so your server stores a folder it cannot read.
- **Password manager**: logins, one-time codes (TOTP) and a generator, with **Android autofill** offering
  them in your other apps and browsers. Every entry is encrypted on your device — the relay holds ciphertext.
- **Bookmark sync**: the companion add-on (Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Brave) keeps bookmarks in step across
  browsers, sealed with the same vault key.
- **Mail**: your own IMAP/SMTP accounts, mirrored as encrypted events so search works without a round trip.

**The AI powerhouse**

- **Chat**: streaming LLM conversations against your own models or any OpenAI-compatible API.
- **Generation**: images, music and video, produced on your own GPU rather than someone's rented one.
- **Private search**: a metasearch engine bundled with your node, with AI overviews and citations.
- **Live streaming**: go live from your camera or screen (NIP-53), and watch other people's streams.
- **Voice and video calls**: 1:1 and group, over WebRTC.

**And a full Nostr client**: feeds, threads, profiles, DMs, communities, mini apps and a web-of-trust relay.

Self-hostable by design — point the app at your own instance; the default is poster.place.
